newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH UTILITY EOP SAYS DELAYS BOND ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH UTILITY EOP SAYS DELAYS BOND ISSUE.

text.p: Czech eletrical utility Elektrary Opatovice (EOP) said on Monday it was delaying the launch of a 2.5 billion crown bond issue because of unfavourable market conditions.
EOP Financial Director Pavel Hypius told Reuters a recent skyrocketing of interest rates caused by a crisis in the crown had created poor conditions for the bonds.
"The issue has been delayed by one month, and then we will see if that is enough," Hypius said.

The Czech central last month hiked its discount rate to 13 percent from 10.5 percent, and its Lombard rate to 50 percent from 14 percent to help support the crown, which was hit hard by a wave of speculative short-selling.
Rates on the interbank money market followed suit, rising to about 45 percent.
Funds from the bonds are to be used to finance restructuring at EOP.
